{"predictors": [
{"name": "R&D Intensity Volatility", "construction": "standard deviation of R&D expense divided by total assets over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with more volatile R&D investments may face greater uncertainty and require a higher return to compensate investors for the risk. This volatility can be a proxy for the firm's ability to adapt to changing market conditions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Pension Plan Underfunding", "construction": "estimated pension liability minus pension plan assets, scaled by total assets", "rationale": "Firms with underfunded pension plans may face significant future liabilities, increasing their financial risk and required return. This underfunding can be a signal of the firm's overall financial health.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Foreign Sales Concentration", "construction": "proportion of total sales generated from foreign countries, calculated over the past 3 years", "rationale": "Firms with a high concentration of foreign sales may be more exposed to exchange rate fluctuations and country-specific risks, requiring a higher return to compensate investors. This concentration can be a proxy for the firm's global diversification.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Employee Growth Rate", "construction": "average annual growth rate of total employees over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with rapidly growing workforces may be experiencing increasing returns to scale or expanding into new markets, leading to higher expected returns. This growth rate can be a signal of the firm's future prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Advertising Expense Persistence", "construction": "autoregressive coefficient from a regression of current advertising expense on past advertising expense, estimated over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with persistent advertising expenses may be building strong brand recognition and customer loyalty, leading to higher expected returns. This persistence can be a proxy for the firm's marketing effectiveness.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Tangible Asset Intensity", "construction": "net property, plant, and equipment divided by total assets", "rationale": "Firms with high tangible asset intensity may be more vulnerable to economic downturns and require a higher return to compensate investors for the risk. This intensity can be a signal of the firm's capital structure.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Accounts Receivable Turnover", "construction": "total sales divided by average accounts receivable, calculated over the past year", "rationale": "Firms with high accounts receivable turnover may be experiencing strong customer demand and efficient working capital management, leading to higher expected returns. This turnover can be a proxy for the firm's operational efficiency.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Reversal", "construction": "change in capital expenditures divided by total assets, calculated over the past year", "rationale": "Firms with large reversals in capital expenditures may be responding to changes in their competitive environment, requiring a higher return to compensate investors for the risk. This reversal can be a signal of the firm's adaptability.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Inventory Growth Rate", "construction": "average annual growth rate of total inventory over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with rapidly growing inventories may be experiencing increasing demand or preparing for future growth, leading to higher expected returns. This growth rate can be a proxy for the firm's future prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Executive Compensation Sensitivity", "construction": "sensitivity of CEO compensation to stock price performance, estimated over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with high executive compensation sensitivity may be more likely to have managers acting in the interests of shareholders, leading to higher expected returns. This sensitivity can be a proxy for the firm's corporate governance.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}
]}
